The paper addresses inverse scattering for multilayered particles illuminated by acoustic or electromagnetic plane waves.
Single-frequency inverse problem (IPS) is practically unresolvable due to non-uniqueness and instability.
Multiple frequencies are required for stable identification of multilayer configurations.
Example configurations Q₁ (2 layers) and Q₂ (3 layers) produced Φ(Q₂)=0.00012 at k₀=3.0, making them indistinguishable.
At k₀=10.0, the same configurations produced Φ(Q₂)=1.4307, clearly distinguishing them.
The best fit functional Φ is defined as the normalized squared difference between computed and observed scattered fields.
The objective function has many narrow local minima with sharp peaks and large gradients.
Gradient-based minimization methods fail for this problem due to the complex landscape.
Powell's Method is used for local minimization without requiring derivative information.
The Reduction Procedure merges adjacent layers with similar refractive indices.
The Reduction Procedure is essential; all numerical experiments failed without it.
The minimization space dimension is chosen a priori as 2M, larger than 2N where N is the unknown number of layers.
The Multilevel Single-Linkage Method (MSLM) combines global random search with local minimization.
MSLM uses clustering with critical distance d_j to avoid redundant local searches.
MSLM iteratively generates batches of L random trial points and combines them into enlarged batches.
The reduced sample H_red contains the γjL points with smallest Φ values from batch H_j.
Deep's Method was tested but failed consistently for this type of problem.
The critical distance d_j in MSLM is calculated using gamma functions and depends on the number of points jL.
MSLM terminates when W_tot < W + 0.5, where W is the number of local minima found.
The one-dimensional minimization uses Brent's method for finding minima along search directions.
The 'turtle' minimization procedure restricts probed points to within distance d_min from the starting configuration.
The admissible set A_adm requires layer radii to be ordered: r₁ ≤ r₂ ≤ ... ≤ r_M.
Refractive indices are bounded: n_low ≤ n_m ≤ n_high based on physical estimates.
The paper uses three frequencies P = {3.0, 6.5, 10.0} in numerical experiments.
The scatterer is modeled as a circle D of radius R with N concentric layers.
